context: a letter from P. L. Sclater, which you are answering
exchanges:
I send you an extract from the minutes of one of our scientific meetings relating to the subject I was speaking of today— I find nothing was said about it in the printed volume of Proceedings—

I find I never answered your letter of the 4th. and now have only to say that Sylvicola aureola may be a distinct species, but it is a close ally of S. æstiva of N . and S. America and perhaps only a “climatic variety” or as the Germans say “climatische Abart”—

The next time I go to the B.M. I will examine Otus galapagoensis Zenaida galapagoensis and S. aureola.

Very faithfully Your’s | P.L Sclater

Very sincere thanks for your kind information, which is very valuable to me.— I asked G. R. Gray about the Otus & Zenaida—but whether he will give me satisfactory information I know not.— I had intended asking you whether the Strix punctatissima & Pyrocephalus nanus differed in any degree whatever, in size & duskiness from the same species on the Mainland. This would be very interesting to me; but I fear I am too troublesome.—

With sincere thanks | Yours very faithfully | Charles Darwin
